name: loatheb
_comment: Level-2 JSON port of the C++ Loatheb strategy (LoathebPositionAction + LoathebChooseTargetAction). Loatheb is a single-phase tank-and-spank, so encounter_active stays true for the whole fight with no blind-spot gaps. NOT PORTED: LoathebGenericMultiplier - json-raid has no multiplier layer. Under .rjson on you therefore lose (a) Necrotic-Aura heal-window gating (healers will try to heal into the aura; the game blocks it ~99% so it's wasted mana/globals, not a wipe) and (b) neglect-threat + formation-move suppression (normal threat applies again - this strat keeps the tank glued to the boss to compensate). .rjson off restores the full C++ behavior. Coords copied verbatim from RaidNaxxBossHelper.h: mainTankPos {2877.57,-3967.00}, rangePos {2896.96,-3980.61}.

rules._comment: Main tank holds Loatheb at the C++ mainTankPos and stays on the boss (attack@1). The tank is excluded from the Spore rule below because IsDps is false for a pure tank, so it never abandons the boss - critical here since json-raid has no neglect-threat multiplier and a wandering tank would drop aggro to a DPS bot.

Ranged + healers stack at the C++ rangePos and stay on the boss. stack_point@3 anchors them there: ranged DPS that also match the dps Spore rule below will nuke a Spore from rangePos when it's in range, but never run across the room (the anchor wins movement). Healers heal via their base strategy; attack@1 is a low-priority filler so they contribute when not casting.

DPS burst the Spore add (entry 16286) the instant one spawns, then fall back to Loatheb. Melee in the pile earn Fungal Bloom (+50% crit) when it dies. select defaults to lowest_hp (kill the add first); the Spore enters combat via SetInCombatWithZone so the default threat-detection sees it immediately. Gated to dps (NOT melee) so the tank is excluded; drops the C++ 1.0y proximity gate so all melee swap on spawn instead of only the adjacent one, and lets ranged help finish the add.
